name: Redemption
description: The possibility of moral and spiritual recovery after sin or suffering
examples: Raskolnikov's redemption through suffering and love (Crime and Punishment)

name: Suffering
description: Physical, emotional, or spiritual pain as path to meaning or growth
examples: Russian literature often presents suffering as redemptive (Dostoevsky, Tolstoy)

name: Faith
description: Religious belief and its role in providing meaning and moral guidance
examples: Alyosha's faith (Brothers Karamazov), Levin's spiritual quest (Anna Karenina)

name: Love
description: Romantic, familial, or spiritual love as transformative force
examples: Tatyana's love (Eugene Onegin), Anna's passion (Anna Karenina)

name: Nihilism
description: Rejection of traditional values and authority
examples: Bazarov (Fathers and Sons), Raskolnikov's theory (Crime and Punishment)

name: Society
description: Social structures, class, and their constraints on individuals
examples: Anna's ostracism (Anna Karenina), Pechorin's alienation (A Hero of Our Time)

name: Fate
description: Question of free will vs predestination
examples: Pierre's search for purpose (War and Peace), Pechorin's fatalism

name: Freedom
examples: Eugene Onegin's rejection of society, Raskolnikov's theory of extraordinary men

name: Mortality
description: Death and the meaning of existence
examples: Prince Andrei's death epiphany (War and Peace), Anna's suicide (Anna Karenina)

name: Alienation
examples: Superfluous man archetype (Pechorin, Onegin), Akaky (The Overcoat)

name: Duty
examples: Tatyana chooses duty over passion (Eugene Onegin)

name: Passion
examples: Anna's passionate love (Anna Karenina), Dmitri's sensuality (Brothers Karamazov)
